column2:
Proxmox’s command-line tool for QEMU/KVM virtual machines. Used alone, it displays usage guidance; supply a subcommand to perform an action, such as qm list. This general command card is distinct from the existing qm list card.
Proxmox VE: Proxmox Virtual Environment, a platform for running virtual computers and containers.
Virtual machine: A software-defined computer with its own operating system.
QEMU: Software that provides virtual computer hardware.
KVM: Kernel-based Virtual Machine, Linux support for hardware-assisted virtualization.
Subcommand: An action word supplied after a program name.

column1:
sudo systemctl is-active networking
Check whether the networking service is active.
column2:
Checks the systemd unit named networking and prints its current state. The exit status is zero when it is active, and nonzero otherwise. This checks that service’s state; use separate checks to confirm network connectivity. The unit may be absent on systems using another network manager.
sudo: Run an authorized command as another user, usually the administrator.
systemd: Linux’s system and service manager.
Unit: A resource managed by systemd, such as a service.
Service: A background program or managed system task.
Exit status: A number returned by a command; zero usually indicates success.

column1:
nmcli device status
List network devices and connection states.
column2:
Shows devices known to NetworkManager, their types, current states and associated connection profiles. Useful for spotting connected, disconnected or unmanaged interfaces.
nmcli: NetworkManager’s command-line interface.
NetworkManager: Software that manages network connections.
Network interface: A physical or virtual connection used for network traffic.
Connection profile: Saved settings for a network connection.
Unmanaged: Not currently controlled by NetworkManager.

column1:
nmcli device disconnect ens18
Disconnect the ens18 network device.
column2:
Asks NetworkManager to disconnect ens18 and prevent further automatic activation on that device until manual intervention. This can immediately interrupt a remote session using ens18. It does not permanently set a profile’s autoconnect property to no. Authorization may be required.
nmcli: NetworkManager’s command-line interface.
NetworkManager: Software that manages network connections.
ens18: The network interface name used in this command.
Activation: Bringing a network connection into use.
Autoconnect: Automatically starting a saved network connection.

column1:
sudo nmcli connection modify ens18 connection.autoconnect no
Stop a saved connection from starting automatically.
column2:
Sets the autoconnect property to no for the connection profile named ens18. Here ens18 must identify a profile, which may have a different name from its device; check nmcli connection show. Changes the saved setting but does not by itself disconnect an active connection.
sudo: Run an authorized command as another user, usually the administrator.
nmcli: NetworkManager’s command-line interface.
NetworkManager: Software that manages network connections.
Connection profile: A named collection of saved network settings.
Autoconnect: Automatically activating a saved connection when suitable conditions exist.
Property: One named setting within a profile.

column1:
nmcli connection show
List saved network connection profiles.
column2:
Lists NetworkManager connection profiles with their names, UUIDs, types and associated devices. Includes inactive profiles; a blank device field can mean the profile is not active. A profile name does not have to match an interface name.
nmcli: NetworkManager’s command-line interface.
NetworkManager: Software that manages network connections.
Connection profile: Saved settings for a network connection.
UUID: Universally Unique Identifier, a long identifier used to distinguish a profile.
Network interface: A physical or virtual network connection.

Prints Enforcing, Permissive or Disabled. Enforcing applies SELinux policy; Permissive records policy violations without blocking them; Disabled means SELinux is off. This reports the current mode and does not change it.
SELinux: Security-Enhanced Linux, a security system that limits what programs and users may access.
Policy: Rules defining which actions are allowed.
Enforcement: Blocking actions that violate the rules.

Displays active swap files and devices, including their type, size, used space and priority. With --show this is an inspection command; it does not enable new swap. No listed entries usually means no swap is active.
Swap: Space used to hold memory pages outside normal working memory.
RAM: Random Access Memory, the working memory used by programs.
Swap file: A regular file used for swap storage.
Priority: A value affecting which swap area is preferred; higher values are used first.

column1:
findmnt /
Show what filesystem is mounted at the root folder.
column2:
Displays the current mount for /, including its source, filesystem type and mount options. The source may be a disk device, logical volume or another kind of storage.
Mount: Make a filesystem accessible at a folder.
/ (root directory): The top-level folder of the Linux file tree.
Filesystem: The structure that organizes files on storage.
Mount options: Settings controlling how a filesystem is accessed.
Logical volume: A virtual storage device built from a pool of disk space.
